title: IndexedDB Persistence
description: Use IndexedDB for large-scale cache persistence in React Query applications.

data.text: IndexedDB is a low-level, transactional database built into every modern browser. Unlike localStorage, it is fully asynchronous, supports structured data and indexes, and can store hundreds of megabytes or more. For React Query apps with large caches â€” think chat histories, document stores, or analytics data â€” IndexedDB is the correct choice.

cards.title: localStorage

cards.title: IndexedDB
cards.description: Asynchronous transactional database with indexes and large capacity.

data.text: React Query provides an async persister for IndexedDB through the `@tanstack/query-async-storage-persister` package. It uses `idb-keyval` under the hood for a simple key-value interface over IndexedDB. Because it is asynchronous, hydration happens after the initial render â€” you should handle this gracefully in your UI.

terms.definition: A tiny library that wraps IndexedDB with a simple Promise-based key-value API.
Restoring the cache from async storage after the initial render, requiring a loading state.

data.text: Because IndexedDB access is asynchronous, the app may render before hydration completes. During this window, the query cache is empty. Use a loading state or skeleton UI to bridge this gap gracefully.

data.title: Async Hydration Note
data.text: The PersistQueryClientProvider handles hydration internally. The loading state example above is illustrative â€” in practice, you can listen to the persister's restore promise or use the onRestore callback.

data.title: Exercise: Migrate from localStorage to IndexedDB
data.description: Your app currently uses localStorage persistence. Migrate it to IndexedDB to support larger datasets. Ensure the app handles async hydration gracefully.
steps: Configure the IndexedDB database name and object store.
Add a loading state that shows while hydration is in progress.
Test with a large dataset (e.g., 1000+ cached items) and verify it persists correctly.
data.expectedOutcome: The app persists and hydrates a large cache using IndexedDB, with no data loss and a smooth loading state.

items.question: Does IndexedDB work in all browsers?
items.answer: IndexedDB is supported in all modern browsers. For older browsers, consider a fallback to localStorage or include an IndexedDB polyfill.

items.question: Will async hydration cause a visible flash?
items.answer: It can, if not handled. Use a loading state or skeleton UI to cover the hydration period. Many apps show cached data immediately and accept that the first paint may use the previous session's data.

items.question: How do I inspect the IndexedDB cache?
items.answer: Open Chrome DevTools â†’ Application â†’ Storage â†’ IndexedDB. You will see your database name and can browse the stored cache entries directly.

data.title: IndexedDB Persistence Key Points
points: IndexedDB handles large datasets far beyond localStorage limits.
Async persistence requires handling the hydration loading window.
Use idb-keyval for a simple Promise-based interface.
Consider fallback to localStorage for older browsers.
data.takeaway: IndexedDB persistence enables rich offline experiences for data-intensive applications.
